The popularity of professional esports has surged in recent years, with fans actively following professional players and teams on social media platforms, with one of the top leagues in North America having teams boasting millions of followers. As the industry continues to grow, there is a strong interest in utilizing data visualization and machine learning techniques to analyze player performance and relationships, with the goal of providing coaches and managers with valuable insights that could potentially enhance team management. However, a significant obstacle hindering this research area is the lack of comprehensive and reliable public datasets that incorporate both performance and relational data, which are typically treated as separate entities. To address this challenge, we have compiled and made available a dataset called TwitchPlayers, consisting of over 100,000 players from the game League of Legends, with a one-year time period, which includes both link and node data derived from Twitter interactions and game statistics. This dataset is suitable for testing embedding algorithms with the aim of producing models similar to TwitchPlayers' actual characteristics.

Our study focuses on the distinction between two theories regarding the $f_X(1500)$ resonance, specifically whether it is a real resonance or a crossover of the $\rho^0(1450)$ state. We gathered experimental data from the Belle collaboration and utilized a neural network to simulate data corresponding to $B^0\to K^+K^-\pi^-$ decays, subsequently analyzing it with an existing likelihood model. Additionally, we employed two different amplitude models and calculated branching fractions and CP-violating asymmetries. Our results indicate that if $f_X(1450)$ represents a real resonance, its contribution to $B^0\to K^+K^-\pi^-$ decays would manifest as an enhancement around the $\rho^0(1450)$ mass without significantly affecting other kinematic distributions. If it is merely a crossover of the $\rho^0(1450)$, its contribution would be too subtle to be detected with the current dataset of $1.86$ pb$^{-1}$. A larger dataset is necessary to make an informed decision on this topic.

Recent observations of extra dimensions in extra spectroscopic dimensions in extra molecular bonds in hadron collisions suggest a possible link to the unknown aspects of our universe. Specifically, researchers are exploring whether adding a new dimension to our three-dimensional space could offer insight into the observed expansion of the universe. They propose that if primordial black holes make up a certain fraction of dark matter, around $10^{-7}$ of it, they could be responsible for this observed expansion. These scientists suggest a new term in Einstein's field equations known as the dark pressure composed of primordial black holes, which accounts for both dark matter and dark energy as properties of primordial black holes. They propose a new conservation law called the conservation of the substance composed of primordial black holes, which includes three parts: the dark matter in our three-dimensional space, the primordial black holes moving through four-dimensional spacetime, and the dark pressure. These scientists also discover that if primordial black holes make up the substance's intrinsic value, which remains constant over time, they could be the key to understanding the overall expansion of our universe. Additionally, researchers are proposing a new concept known as the dark fluid which emerges when primordial black holes make up the substance's dominant fraction, constituting more than $10^{-7}$ of it. They propose that if primordial black holes make up the substance's dominant fraction, dark matter and dark energy would be intrinsic properties of primordial black holes, and thus could be observed directly using a gravitational wave detector.

Force control systems with series elastic actuators are highly advantageous for their light weight and precise force output, making them suitable for collaborative operations with humans; however, traditional transmission force estimation methods struggle with accuracy and stability due to factors like the low stiffness of the elastic component, system integration, and external influences. This study introduces an innovative transmission force estimation technique that leverages the characteristics of series elastic actuators for more effective performance. A theoretical model and stability analysis were conducted to validate the method, which was then experimentally tested on a test bench featuring the actuator and an elastic element. Results show that this new approach outstandingly outperforms conventional transmission force estimation techniques in terms of accuracy and performance.

Self-assembled structures called monolayered rafts that form on surfaces can
create functional devices when their working properties are utilized. These rafts
are similar to biological rafts that appear in cell membranes. In this study, we
employed an advanced microscopy technique to examine the defects and boundaries
within 2D rafts made of particles that have an affinity for each other. As a result
of our investigations, we found that certain boundary shapes, especially those in
the shape of triangles, can cause certain particles to be left out, and that
sudden shifts in particles can occur at linear sections of these boundaries. When
we tried to simulate these boundaries with varying strengths, we found that
particles would stick together more firmly when the boundaries were thick, and that
these boundary movements can occur suddenly, which can cause the rafts to collapse
under certain conditions. The data that we collected from our experiments can be
used to better understand the nature of these boundaries and can aid researchers
in utilizing the properties of rafts to create functional devices when they
self-assemble without outside intervention.

We investigated a lattice SU(Nc) gauge theory in 3D that includes interactions for scalars belonging to the fundamental representation of SU(Nc), and we determined the nature of its non-perturbative phase transition. By analyzing the phase plot derived from the phase ratio of a polyakov loop, we found evidence of an intermediate phase, characterized as a Higgs phase, between a confining phase and a Coulomb phase. This intermediate phase's size varies with the number of colors, becoming more pronounced for larger values of Nc. Additionally, we studied the spectrum of screened color charges as an indicator for the phase structure, which supported our phase ratio findings, and we suggest that lattice simulations with lattice spacing matching, could provide more insight into the nature of the phase transition.

An autonomous marine robot navigation requires accounting for environmental disturbances, such as ocean currents, that can alter the robot's motion. To address this, this study investigates temporal variation in ocean currents and develops a Sparse Gaussian Process model to predict spatial variation as the robot moves through different areas. A real marine robot is utilized for validating the proposed approach, with experimental results demonstrating the SPGLSS model's effectiveness in efficiently learning the robot's dynamic motion patterns and successfully predicting its navigation. A data visualization is also provided to illustrate the learning process and the model's impact on the robot's navigation capabilities.

This paper identifies the minimum number of comparisons required for sorting within specific constraints, focusing on tasks related to sorting given $k$ numbers. We determine the precise minimum comparisons required in three scenarios: when the numbers are 2-knuxial, when they are addition-chain-ordered, and when they are $2^k$-knuxial. Our research also establishes a fundamental lower bound of $2k$ bits for representing any sorting network with a fixed depth of $2k$. This result has a direct implication, showing that sorting networks of a fixed depth $2k$ cannot efficiently represent all possible permutations of $2k$ numbers. Notably, this indicates that certain types of sorting networks, such as those based on bit-sliced networks, 0-1 orderable networks, and permutation networks, cannot sort even a linear number of $2k$-nuxial numbers.

We employ the relativistic Euler equations to explore non-uniform gas and fluid-critical dust combinations under static conditions, without assuming equilibrium conditions. Using a suitable coordinate system, we derive the governing differential equation for both types of configurations and generate numerical solutions for gas supported by pressure and dust configurations supported by gravity alone. From these solutions, we derive the mass function and compactness of these configurations, supported by various equations of state, and visualize their profiles. Our findings reveal that non-uniform stars held together by gas pressure can exhibit exotic phenomena such as infinite densities at finite radii, characteristic of singularities, whereas configurations consisting of fluid and dust can lead to infinite densities at the surface, suggesting the possibility of boundaries between regions of different densities.

We used N-body simulations to study the formation of spiral patterns in a simulated galaxy that resembled the Milky Way, consisting of four distinct component populations. Our simulations showed that a high angular momentum caused by a bar or near it was often responsible for creating an "inner-helix" structure in the central region of the galaxy. A two-scale bar, if present, could also lead to the same effect. A prominent super spiral was usually made possible by a bar that exhibited an m=2 harmonic twist in its outer region, and often a multi-armed bar was observed before a multi-helix galaxy formed. Similarly, an outer bar with a short angular momentum timescale and a primary bar often resulted in a galaxy with an inner-helix structure. A stable, elongated disk with a longer bar timescale often produced an "outer-helix" structure, and it was often made possible either by a long bar with a high-multiplicity twist or by a secondary, shorter bar near it. A dense bulge often restricted the extension of a long bar, and it was often responsible itself for a secondary bar, often leading to an "inner-helix" galaxy. A secondary, shorter bar often created an "outer-helix" galaxy, and it was often made possible either by a long bar with a high multiplicity twist or, and often, it was observed that an outer bar did produce a multi-helix galaxy.

We investigated how initial magnetic fields at $z=1$ affect galaxy collisions. Using the ENZO-$B$ simulator, we ran 100 high-resolution simulations with 100 magnetic field strengths spanning from $10^{-16}$ G to $10^{-9}$ G. Our results show that even the weakest magnetic fields steer a significant portion of galaxies' gas, up to 30 percent, into spiral patterns. These magnetic fields can generate significant turbulence in galaxies gas, contributing to angular momentum mixing and contributing to galaxy collisions morphological transformations. As a result, stronger magnetic fields can accelerate the transition from spiral to galaxy morphology. Furthermore, stronger magnetic fields can produce more hot gas and stellar streams due to enhanced collisions between galaxies. These features can be found in significant number of galaxy collisions and merging galaxies and can be used to guide future semi-analytical and semi empirical models of galaxy collisions and mergers to better understand the role magnetic fields play in galaxy collisions and mergers.

Recent severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 pandemic outbreaks have highlighted the necessity for rapid and reliable diagnosis, where radiologists, who use chest CT scans to quickly assess and classify the severity of infection, may face difficulties due to limited training time and accuracy. To address this challenge, our goal is to develop a chest CT classification method that accurately identifies COVID-19 infection severity. Building upon a foundational classification model, we introduce a novel technique to enhance the data efficiency and generalization capabilities of pre-trained neural networks. This innovative approach combines self-supervised learning principles, data augmentation strategies, and contradictionary supervision to refine the classification accuracy for chest CT scans. Our comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, yielding substantial improvements in infection severity classification performance. Notably, we observe up to a 13.4% reduction in errors when assessing limited datasets, and a 7.57% reduction in errors in real-world applications.

Most current systems for correcting grammatical errors rely on large amounts of annotated data within a specific domain. We explored a novel approach, utilizing large foundation models in combination with few-shot domain adaptation techniques in order to create a system capable of handling other languages and domains with minimal reliance on annotated training data. We implemented a multi-task meta-learning framework, enabling a single system to handle multiple languages and domains simultaneously, requiring only a small amount of annotated data from new languages and domains. Rather than treating each new domain or language as completely independent, this approach leverages shared knowledge across different domains and languages to facilitate efficient transfer learning. We demonstrated that our system could rectify grammatical errors in Chinese and Japanese, and even added support for Low Resource African languages Swahili and Shona. Furthermore, we developed systems for English and other European languages within the domains of General, Medical, and Customer Reviews. Our results indicate that our two-shot multi-domain SWA-Edit system achieved an F0.5 score of 0.8676, significantly outperforming large foundation models in both Low Resource and Multi-Domain settings.

Firms frequently release financial data by publishing averages of totals from financial statements. Because these averages are often rounded to the nearest whole number, some information is lost, affecting the accuracy of inferred totals. Researchers have consistently tackled this issue of data quality, yet they have neglected to address the underlying uncertainty created by this rounding practice. We aim to rectify this by applying average-based accounting data, taking into account any introduced ambiguity. We devise a average-based panel data model, accounting for the ambiguity and utilizing it to enhance estimation of unobserved variables. We validate the model's effectiveness against traditional linear models and demonstrate that it can yield more precise estimates of hidden factors when average-based data is used, both theoretically and practically.

Researchers investigated the single-crystal magnetism of quasi-two-dimensional centered honeycomb GdInO$_3$ by conducting bulk ac susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and M-H hysteresis measurements.  A hexagonal structure was found in the Gd subsystem, with six-fold symmetry.  Exchange interactions within the honeycomb lattice cause a magnetic phase transition at $T_N$ = 2.04 K.  At zero field, a six-fold magnetic symmetry persists in the ordered state, and a remnant magnetization of $0.004\mu_B/Gd$ exists in the saturated state.  A spiral structure was also found in the Gd subsystem when subjected to a 2 T transverse field.  Further, a quarter-polarization was observed in a 50 T longitudinal field.

We are examining the connection between cooperative and non-cooperative games in the context of problems that involve allocating non-transferable items to agents who are acting strategically, where a Pure Nash Equilibrium (PNE) represents a form of stability. Our research reveals the limitations of PNE in representing certain objectives, and we establish a connection to cooperative games through the concept of equity. Specifically, we establish that in many situations, PNE can result in pronounced inequalities, and we establish that it is extremely difficult to find an equilibrium where no player is significantly disadvantaged, and we establish that it is also very difficult to obtain an equitable allocation in which no player is significantly disadvantaged. In addition, we establish that it is significantly more difficult to find an equilibrium where no player is significantly disadvantaged, and we establish that it is significantly more difficult to find an equitable allocation in which no player is significantly disadvantaged. As a contrast, we establish that it is easily achievable to find a "bound-aware" version of PNE, and we establish that it is easily achievable to find an equitable allocation that takes into account these limits. As another contrast, we establish that it is also achievable to find a Pareto-optimal version of PNE, and we establish that it is also easily achievable to find an equitable allocation in which no player is significantly disadvantaged. The prevalent view that unsupervised domain adaptation maps source and target data points one-to-one seems limiting for complex, high-dimensional real-world scenarios. We challenge this perspective and propose a novel concept: stochastic domain adaptation, which maps source and target data to multiple target data points. In experiments on image style transfer and handwritten digit recognition from real images, stochastic domains outperform traditional deterministic domains consistently. Notably, we achieved state-of-the-art results using stochastic domains in real-to-handwritten digit recognition recognition, surpassing previous records by 3.94% in accuracy. Our code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/zhengqian1994/Stochastic_Domain_Adaptation.

We have discovered an ultra-stable, gas-rich disk structure in galaxy UGC 8839,
which exhibits two nearly symmetric and elongated lobes rotating independently,
rotating in the same direction but with different speeds and orientations.
By analyzing kinematic data, we determined that the disk has an inner major axis
rotating at a period of approximately 24 days and an inclination of around 45 degrees.
Further investigation using major axis fitting and residual analysis revealed that
UGC 8839 may consist of three distinct components: its central bulge, this ultra-stable
disk, and a slowly rotating outer disk. Additionally, fitting a disk model to the SFR
map showed that the disk model and the galaxy's central bulge rotate out of phase,
with an inclination of approximately 30 degrees. These findings suggest that the
ultra-stable disk's orientation is likely unrelated to the galaxy's central bulge or
its outer disk counterpart.

Scientists are utilizing paleo-detectors, which analyze stone paleo-detectors for traces of decaying primordial matter particles, to place extremely sensitive bounds on these particles' interaction strength and interaction cross-section with the dark matter nucleus. However, this approach's potential can be maximized by incorporating a variety of paleo-detector materials and taking advantage of the different targets, overwhelming flux, and temperature-dependent thresholds that stone detectors experience. We simulate these factors to create comprehensive predictions for Paleodetector Direct Dark Matter searches, which can be compared with current and upcoming experiments, revealing that paleo-detectors have the potential to provide the most stringent dark matter parameter space insights globally, rather than just improving sensitivity to these experiments.

This paper introduces a novel differential privacy technique, DP-Sync, for safeguarding an outsourced database system from a malevolent cloud service provider. The study addresses the issue of a hacker who can access data and infer internal system information, particularly when the system employs basic encryption and trend analysis. The researcher introduces DP-Sync by incorporating a unique combination of cryptographic methods and integrating the differential privacy technique, F-PS, into the system. DP-Sync utilizes a novel variant of sync hash to reduce computational overhead and replaces traditional random number generators with differential privacy-protected hash functions. The result is a more efficient and data-security-focused system that minimizes performance impacts while significantly enhancing data protection against a malevolent cloud service provider.

Machine learning techniques have been widely utilized in feature selection for enhancing information extraction and filtering from deceptive content, such as spam and fake news. While previous studies focused on singular evaluation methods, like stability tests, they overlooked the influence of a classifier's algorithm on reliability. This study examines whether state-of-the-art ensemble learning algorithm, specifically the Random Forest, can offer robust performance across multiple evaluation criteria, including accuracy, F-score, and consistency. Our comprehensive testing utilized five diverse datasets and 15 classification models to compare our proposed method with existing feature significance assessment techniques. Findings demonstrate that the random forest-based approach not only matches but also surpasses the performance of traditional methods. Furthermore, we investigated the capability of generating high-quality adversarial examples using this ensemble method. Our results indicate that only 4% of deceptive samples can be successfully classified as benign after being perturbed by the random forest model, thereby confirming its exceptional consistency. To address concerns regarding data diversity, we incorporated the least-squares method into the ensemble, which yielded a 1% improvement in evaluating deceptive samples. This research provides a thorough assessment of feature significance evaluation through a reliable random forest approach and its potential application in enhancing machine learning-based classification.

Minimally invasive surgery has been greatly enhanced by automatic surgical tool identification and tracking systems using computer vision technology. Traditional method-based approaches achieve high accuracy but lack flexibility and require extensive computation. This study explores the potential of deep learning methods to create more efficient and adaptable tool identification and tracking models in minimally invasive surgery. Top-performing deep learning models were evaluated and a flexible tool tracking system was developed through the combination of Bayesian inference and model enhancement techniques. The newly developed models demonstrated competitive accuracy on publicly available datasets NTU-Surg and CHU-Lyon, outperforming or matching the results of highly rated traditional method-based approaches on both datasets. The experiment outcomes indicate the promise of deep learning methods in achieving high accuracy model surgical tool identification and tracking, offering improved efficiency and adaptability for surgical tools analysis.

Existing cross-camera identity recognition systems often rely on paired training data, but such pairs are notoriously difficult to label on large-scale datasets. To address this limitation, we collected an extensive paired training dataset for a popular benchmark, PAVIA, comprising 4200 pairs across 350 subjects, and expanded it to 7 days of data. Leveraging color and spatial features, a baseline system achieved a remarkable 59.3% accuracy. Building on this, we applied contrastive learning using only our paired data, and significantly improved accuracy to 81.5%, our proposed system represents the SOTA performance using only paired data, and outperforms top-enterance systems on the PAVIA dataset.

This paper introduces a novel class of models called achieved threshold measurement GARCH (ATMGARCH) to predict tail risk in financial markets and uses a Bayesian approach for estimation. A ATMGARCH model captures asymmetric volatility clustering in the stock market and forecasts Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) with high accuracy. High-dimensional variables are incorporated into the ATMGARCH model to enhance its predictive capabilities. A Reliability-Enforcing Neural Network (RENN) is then used in a Markov Switching ATMGARCH-neural network (MSATMGARCH-NEURAL) model to identify the most effective feature set. Empirical results show that the MSATMGARCH-NEURAL model outperforms both traditional Bayesian ATMGARCH and standard GARCH models in terms of VaR and CVaR accuracy.

A new method is introduced to compute the robust parameter $\alpha$ from pulsar timing data, with the aim of mitigating the influence of outliers on estimation results. This parameter is a crucial component of rate stability characterization and has recently gained significant importance due to its application in selecting appropriate frequency domain stability metrics for use in pulsar beam steering applications. The proposed approach involves a transformation of time series data into residual sequences, from which various methods of moment calculation can be employed to estimate $\alpha$. The results of the initial implementation indicate that the results obtained from these adjusted calculations align with previously established methods based on time series analysis, and provide greater protection against the effects of data outliers. Furthermore, comparing different moment calculation techniques yields varying outcomes, necessitating further research to identify the most optimal approach.

A theoretical investigation involving two current correlations in real-time scalar QED is conducted, using pions as non-relativistic, Cooper pair-like entities. The study demonstrates the generation of electric fields within a pion and confirms that the pion decays when currents are switched off. The emergence of magnetic moments in pions is demonstrated by introducing external electromagnetic fields. The validity of a relativistic extension is shown to be dependent on a ratio that must remain much less than one. The available data support a proposed extension of the model to a relativistic regime.

Low-mass pre-main sequence stars typically exhibit bursts of light caused by changes in mass accretion rates. These bursts are usually rapid and allow for accurate determination of mass accretion rates. However, some stars, like XX Cha, are capable of sustaining prolonged periods of activity that significantly affect the lower boundaries of $ \dot{M} $ ranges for the entire XX Cha subpopulation. As a result, current research must account for exceptional cases such as XX Cha to gain a comprehensive understanding of accretion rates. As more data is collected from the VLT in the coming years, the more rare events will become increasingly common as they do now contribute a significant percentage to their respective bins. Moreover, these fluctuations in activity are highly apparent when observed from a visual perspective. In order to accurately assess the full spectrum of activity rates, it is essential to consider not just the most active and typical stars but also those with less intense activity.

We examine a poorman's version of Mulligan's 'inequity of chance' concept, which shows that agents may feel dissatisfaction when they observe others receiving beneficial opportunities more frequently. According to this model, opportunity share disparities can lead to dissonance, prompting agents to adjust their behavior in an effort to regain balance. We also present an indirect form of income redistribution, where individuals reallocate income based on the dissonance arising from opportunity disparities both of them experience. This approach is tested empirically using a laboratory setting, where we find support for our equilibrium predictions regarding the dissonance experienced, the opportunity sharing behavior, and the income reallocation.

The intricate interplay between data, algorithmic models, and hyperparameter settings in machine learning can lead to difficult-to-debug issues when the expected output is not achieved. This paper introduces the concept of end-to-end machine learning workflow analysis and proposes Data Troubleshooting with Shapley Significance (DTSS) to identify contributing factors to poor model performance. By extending the End-to-End Machine Learning (E2EML) framework, we treat a machine learning model as a black box and treat both data and hyperparameter variations as input to be analyzed for their impact on the predicted result. We leverage the End-Node Importance (ENI) method from the E2EML framework to efficiently compute the Shapley value for each data point, taking into account model structure, hyperparameter configuration, and data. We showcase the effectiveness of DTSS through real-world experiments and additional analyses, demonstrating its ability to pinpoint underfitted and overfitting models, as well as data labeling errors.

We investigated nearly 900 galaxy clusters in the MAVERIC survey to explore possible connections between gamma-rays and radio emissions originating from their central galaxies. Some of these clusters contain "low-morphology" galaxies, characterized by weak or absent star formation and reduced radio emissions. In contrast, "high-morphology" galaxies display active central regions with significant radio emissions. We analyzed a subset of 45 galaxy clusters to examine their dynamics and the emissions originating from their cores. Through time-lapse observations spanning 11 years, we monitored 25 of these clusters and discovered that 22 of them contain galaxies with distinct "bath-tub curves" in their core dynamics. Additionally, some of these clusters exhibit significant radio emissions, while others show negligible or no radio emissions. We evaluated 9 pairs of galaxy clusters that differed only in their central regions, in terms of magnetic fields, gamma-rays, and cosmic rays, and found substantial discrepancies in their characteristics. We inferred that magnetic fields do not significantly influence the dynamics of these cores, while star formation plays a crucial role in generating significant cosmic rays, which in turn may be converted into radio emissions via the synchrotron self-Compton scattering of cosmic rays.

Reconstructing corrupted hypergraphs from incomplete data is challenging due to the complex relationships between vertices. Current methods first convert hypergraphs to graphs by computing pairwise connections, but this conversion loses certain information and requires a computationally expensive process. In response, we propose a novel graph-based approach that directly uses a corrupted hypergraph, accounting for unobserved vertices and edges. Our method can incorporate an initial prediction from a pre-trained model to enhance accuracy and efficiency. A new model called Guided Hypergraph Restoration is presented, featuring a novel guided hyperedge propagation layer to reconstruct the corrupted data. Experimental results on multiple datasets show significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods.

We employ an entropy-based method to automatically identify directional discharges within laser microcavities, eliminating the need for arbitrary thresholds or manual selection. By analyzing entropy maps, we determine the region of directional discharges that minimizes total system entropy, signaling a shift from a high entropy state to a low entropy state. This method is utilized to experimentally determine the threshold current of a sulfurized silicon microcavity laser, and also helps in pinpointing the optimal gain function and directionality of the emitted light.

Raman scattering from a light-clocked thermal atomic ensemble enables precise time-keeping and enhanced measurements by presenting both clock atoms with a coherent light pulse. However, when assessing the clock's stability and accuracy, it is crucial to understand how atomic fluctuations affect the light and whether the atomic collective behavior can be decoupled from the light field using quantum non-demolition measurements. This study presents quantum non-Gaussian photon counting measurements that reveal the atomic number distribution and provide a picture of the atomic ensemble's momentum space. These measurements exhibit super-Poissonian photon counting with a negative binomial distribution, indicating a collective atomic interaction and potential for meeting the standard quantum limit. Octupon numbers extracted from measurements show thermal atomic fluctuations but decouple from clock preparation, paving the way for better clocks through QRNG-based atomic sampling.

Existing offline reinforcement learning approaches for multiple interacting agents can't properly handle agents that don't actively engage with each other. To bridge this gap, we introduce OFFMARSE, a novel framework that lets students learn from experiences resulting from collective agent interaction. OFFMARSE lets each student separately analyze potential interactions, pinpointing useful knowledge and incorporating it into their individual policies. We tested this framework in a benchmark environment and found substantial improvements in learners' agent performance when they used knowledge from positive interactions.

We introduce a novel approach for aligning 2D/3D megavoltage images that employs two separate Convolutional Neural Networks, achieving sub-optimal overlap efficiently. This method utilizes the clinical alignment tool's objective function as a criterion rather than the optimal circle size, reducing computation time. By training the 3D registration network with pre-calculated shifts from the 2D/3D alignment, we minimize the necessity for extensive data augmentation and achieve superior results compared to unconstrained counterparts. Our minimal dataset of approximately 20 images proves sufficient for both 2D/3D and 3D/3D registrations, demonstrating the robustness of our proposed method.

Single-particle entanglement generates genuine nonlocal effects similar to single-particle guidance. In order to quantify single-particle entanglement, we introduce a framework inspired by entanglement witnesses. Under this framework, we find that, despite appearing paradoxical, the single-particle guidance phenomenon arises from single-particle entanglement. Consequently, single-particle entanglement is essential for single-particle guidance to occur. Our theory is validated experimentally using optical setups, employing entangled photons capable of exhibiting single-particle guidance. Additionally, we propose optical configurations intended to experimentally establish single-particle entanglement and its impact on measurement outcomes. These experiments use optical circuits to demonstrate increased single-particle entanglement, alongside enhanced single-particle guidance effects.

As self-driving vehicles approach, they promise to significantly improve traffic management through intelligent transportation systems (ITS). However, several challenges arise when creating an effective and secure ITS, one of which is privacy concerns. To address this, federated learning (FL) has been introduced to enable updated and personalized ITS while preserving user data. Despite (FL)'s benefits, its adoption remains limited due to inherent vulnerabilities, necessitating the integration of emerging technologies like blockchain to mitigate these issues. This review systematically explores recent studies on ITS and develops a federated learning framework for self-driving vehicles, analyzing its potential benefits as well as (FL)'s intrinsic flaws in detail.

V392 Persei, a well-known dwarf nova that experienced a remarkable outburst in November 2022, exhibited characteristics of both classical and recurrent novae. Observations following the event's peak showed a powerful and unusual emission in X-rays and a relatively weaker optical luminosity, which is typical of type 1 classical novae but with additional features. V392 Persei also displayed a rapid early decline in the optical light, with an effective decay rate of 1.4, which is faster than most type 1 novae but slower than type 2 novae. V392 Persei's optical and X-ray outburst did not exhibit the key features of type 2 novae, including the absence of subluminal wind acceleration and the absence of iron line-driven shocks. V392 Persei is also notably different from other small-novalike X-ray binary systems. Instead, it most closely resembles a small fraction of $\gamma$-ray luminous classical novae and possibly some recurrent novae. V392 Persei's $\gamma$-ray and X-ray emissions are believed to be linked to the interaction between a rapidly expanding, high-velocity nova wind and the companion star's low-luminosity accretion disk or magnetic field. V392 Persei's $\gamma$-ray and X-ray light curves are indicative of different dynamics than those seen in typical type 2 novae. Instead,

To maintain robust error correction, the necessary number of faulty components should be as low as possible relative to the total number of building blocks, yet the ideal configuration would achieve this efficiency without relying on the scaling of size. Using more complex, larger-scale operations on multiple parts at once could significantly improve the performance of quantum memory operations but requires a detailed analysis of their benefits and limitations. By integrating two component operations into the toric code framework, we demonstrate a substantial increase in the code's distance relative to the number of components, resulting in more efficient performance, a significant improvement over using only two-component operations, and access to logically stable states even when two-component operations are prone to failure, in contrast to needing perfect single-component operations for the toric code's performance to match that of multi-component operations.

Orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) is a key multiple access technique used in modern mobile communication standards like LTE and 5G LTE. In order to minimize the overhead associated with random access procedures, precoding is employed to improve spectral efficiency and reduce latency in the connected state. However, the complexity of optimizing precoder selection increases significantly in this mode, particularly in systems without uplink downlink feedback. This research presents an approach to streamline precoder choice by drawing from the principles of Gaussian mixture models. A codebook of codebooks is created by iteratively updating a set of codebooks, which serves as an optimized lookup table for rapid precoder selection in the presence of channel state information. This pre-computed codebook of codebooks is fed into a feedback system that uses an index to indicate the desired codebook, its location within that codebook, and the reliability of the process. Simulations show a substantial improvement in system performance, with up to a 2 dB gain in achievable sum rate over existing methods. Notably, this approach requires only a one-time codebook creation, which can be hardcoded into user equipment, thus allowing for efficient and low-complexity operation.

A two-dimensional fluid system on a rotating and magnetized torus is examined within the context of the 3D Hofstadter model. Our numerical simulations reveal the persistence of a complex, chaotic surface current that resists disintegration due to its system's unique geometry. This robust nonequilibrium phenomenon can be harnerved to create long-lasting patterns of light and heat on the torus's outer wall.

Bondi mass shedding by black holes can be accelerated through merging events and物质 intake. We analyzed the pace at which this mass loss can occur by using Event Horizon Telescope observations of M87* and immediate surroundings. Our study took into account the documented changes in image brightness, overall brightness, and photon flux seen in the observations. We discovered a significant constraint on how quickly the black hole's mass loss can occur, ruling out approximately 42% of hypothetical models of an extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole at the observed frequency. Moreover, we established a corresponding limit on the charge-to-mass ratio that could be potentialy probed by future observations of this black hole at a less confident confidence level.

We examine how binary mergers in nuclear star clusters affect gravitational wave signals. Using N-body simulations that account for general relativity and gravitational wave dynamics, we observe that most massive stars quickly move to the center of globular clusters, forming a dense central disk or remnant cluster.

In this environment, many massive binaries produce significant gravitational waves. These waves can stay within the cluster, generating a population of stellar black holes that further concentrate due to gravitational radiation.

We investigate various scenarios in a range of cluster types and initial mass ratios. The resulting signals from these mergers can contribute to the gravitational wave background detected by LISA, LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA, and their successor detectors. Notably, we find distinct patterns of mergers occurring within nuclear star clusters compared to other environments.

Nuclear star clusters may host distinct populations of massive stars, particularly those in the inner regions of galaxies. Consequently, they offer a diverse range of mergers that can significantly influence the gravitational wave background.

To better understand this, we develop tools for predicting the gravitational wave signal from stellar mergers in general cases, providing estimates for the amplitude of the gravitational wave background in specific nuclear star cluster environments.

Gamma-Ray Bursts remain a mystery in astrophysics, and detecting gravitational wave signals from neutron star mergers necessitates ruling out GRB sources. However, identifying the precise location and characteristics of a GRB in large-scale surveys can be challenging due to limited onboard processing capabilities and sensor memory. In this paper, we propose a method to simulate the full GECAM onboard system on a mobile device, which can not only reproduce GRB triggers but also demonstrate real-world applicability for future similar detectors. We propose designing a dual-screen mobile Gamma-Ray Burst simulator based on the GECAM design, incorporating a VR head-set for an immersive experience. To evaluate our proposal, we conducted a comprehensive evaluation of the mobile GRB simulator by collecting and analyzing user feedback, resulting in a more intuitive and efficient system that can effectively contribute to future GRB research and development.

This article investigates how linear semigroups of polynomial mappings impact the small-BMOA and standard BMOA spaces of analytic functions on the unit disk, focusing on their associated Dirichlet-type spaces. The article establishes precise conditions under which influence remains consistent and provides a basis for which impact is integral to a specific functional sector of BMOA. Furthermore, it derives integral representation formulas for the linear operators in question and identifies the precise Dirichlet-type spaces where these operators map onto small-BMOA-like spaces.

It is widely assumed that the gap between the scientific output and the knowledge quantity grows as the science system expands. To test this hypothesis, we developed a method to quantify knowledge in a specific scientific domain by analyzing its written text and discovered that it does not consistently match the growth rate of publications or citations. Specifically, we found that the increase in publications and citations received by a science field does not always result in the same growth rate as the knowledge quantity. As an example, we observed that artificial intelligence and machine learning showed a greater knowledge growth rate than biology, although the latter is often considered more advanced. To address this discrepancy, we introduced the concept of "publication efficiency," which measures the balance between a field's growth rate and knowledge quantity. We found that this efficiency fluctuates over time and can be influenced by various factors, including the field's stage of development, its inherent complexity, external demand, and supply-chain issues. Notably, we discovered that the growth of start-up companies in artificial intelligence and machine learning was significantly higher than in biology, due to the superior performance and versatility of these fields in developing intelligent systems.

In the context of dual-hop wireless communication systems that utilize adaptive forwarding relays, a problem arises where a malicious actor positioned strategically between source and destination can interfere with the security of the system by disrupting the signal strength ratio between source and interferer. To tackle this issue, we propose a joint optimization approach targeting the subcarrier assignment, power distribution, and signal positioning of the source, destination, and malicious actor. Aimed at maximizing the system's security capacity, this approach considers ensuring end-to-end link stability. Arelaxing of the problem, coupled with an efficient algorithm for local optimal solution, facilitates its resolution. Through simulation, we demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly surpasses fixed frequency allocation and optimal power strategies, particularly when utilizing a limited number of subcarriers. Furthermore, we show that an optimally positioned malicious actor amplifies our proposed scheme in comparison to an omni-directionally positioned actor.

Two-dimensional systems with robust edge currents due to large bulk gaps are uniquely suited for placing quantum electrodynamics on transitions that maintain their direction. Such systems, when paired with a non-dissipative two-level system, exhibit decoupled photon states that do not interfere with each other. This level of isolation allows them to interact selectively with one of the electrons, while also providing access to multiple, independent communication channels. A mathematical model incorporating a randomized Griffiths term captures both the system's robust topology and the coupling of light to matter. Numerical simulations reveal that decoupling is maintained even in a noisier environment with multiple scattering events. Furthermore, the addition of a controllable, non-random component expands this analogy to include applications in quantum information technology. Ultimately, topologically protected setups provide an ideal environment for studying coherent light-matter interactions.

Automated driving technology has rapidly evolved and is set to revolutionize the automotive industry, making it crucial to develop and refine predictive management systems for automated vehicles. These systems can optimize traffic flow and enhance safety at traffic lights in areas where automated drivers still navigate in a mixed traffic environment. A key aspect of this prediction involves incorporating the complex human behavior patterns into modeling processes, however, behavior often leads to automating drivers making suboptimal decisions and potentially causing severe accidents and disruptions at traffic lights. Consequently, it is essential to develop predictive models that take into account behavior and can offer the best management strategies for automated vehicles, balancing safety and efficiency concerns. This paper aims to create a comprehensive predictive framework for managing automated vehicles at traffic lights that can model behavior and utilize historical data to predict future movements. Our proposed framework utilizes machine learning techniques to model automated drivers and develops a advanced simulation technique to predict their response to signal timing and surrounding factors. To predict future movements of automated vehicles approaching the junction, we also developed a novel method called N-Trail which significantly outperforms existing techniques in accuracy. Our framework also includes a safety-conscious model that automatically adjusts the automated vehicle's behavior to prevent severe accidents and traffic disruptions at traffic lights. To validate the efficacy of our predictive framework, we designed a realistic simulation experiment that mimics a real-world scenario and analyzed the results. Our findings indicate that including the behavior model in the framework can enhance safety and traffic efficiency, however, it also leads to automating drivers modifying their

The breakthrough achieved by surpassing average rewards of one in text-based game environments signifies a significant milestone for agents interacting with complex systems. This paper introduces an accelerated text-based game interface, built upon initial open-source frameworks, that dramatically improves simulation speed while maintaining consistency. By replacing random access memory access during world updates with efficient alternative methods, the proposed interface achieves a tenfold increase in simulation speed. As a result, we observe substantial advancements while utilizing state-of-the-art algorithms requiring enhanced simulation speeds for effective decision-making. These findings include recovering human-like performance in classic puzzles, recovering a rating system on difficult games, solving them without visual aids, and discovering improved agent scores across multiple benchmarks.

Deep learning models such as Recurrent Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks are highly effective at recognizing patterns in time-series video data but often come with高昂的计算成本. This research leverages tensor decomposition, specifically HTD, to adapt these learning models for efficient pattern recognition. By fusing matching frames instead of processing them sequentially, the algorithm significantly reduces computational demands, resulting in significantly fewer non-zero parameters and improved calculation efficiency. Empirical tests demonstrate the proposed method's ability to accurately classify patterns while outperforming traditional deep learning techniques in energy efficiency. To further optimize the HTD-RNN approach, a specialized hardware accelerator called FADE was designed and built, featuring innovative designs for tensor decomposition and MLP operations that result in exceptional energy performance. Feedback from the hardware development process also led to a customized loss function and an adapted optimization technique, specifically the Conjugate Gradient method, which together enabled the creation of a unique deep learning model called HTLML-CIFAR10. Final tests show the HTD-RNN and FADE system to be highly energy-efficient, achieving energy performances of 1.05 GJ per million samples and 0.15 Wh per million samples, respectively, significantly surpassing even the original deep learning models.

Restricted Data Learning in NLP occurs when a model is trained to learn a target language without access to gold-standard target language examples, but can access related source language data and universal prior information. This study examines RDL from a source and prior perspective and investigates the relative worth of additional information by conducting a series of experiments. Our research reveals that (1) a greater amount and depth of related source information leads to a significant enhancement in target language performance; and (2) incorporating related source information along with universal prior knowledge is more effective than relying solely on prior information. Notably, a degree of target task specificity is required to fully utilize prior information to prevent model over-smoothing. Lastly, a degree of target task difficulty is necessary to see a notable RDL benefit.

We disprove the claims from the paper arXiv:1209.2784v2 which suggested that the convexity of global charged conformal weights $\Delta$ held true for all intermediate central charges $c_\text{int}$ between the critical value $\sigma \approx 0.47$ and the maximum possible value $c_\text{max}=4$. Our analysis reveals violations of this behavior for certain values of $c_\text{int}$, and we establish that the relevant convex hull consists of four distinct segments, characterized by specific intervals of $c_\text{int}$ and the corresponding minimum charged conformal weights.

To adapt the quantum imaginary duration evolution method for handling systems divided into multiple independent regions, a new approach called multi-region quantum imaginary duration evolution is introduced. This approach creates an effective, coupled system that evolves in imaginary time, effectively capturing the ground states of the original, separate systems. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through applications such as obtaining the spin correlation and effective interactions in the Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain, and recovering the effective Hofstadter butterfly in a toroidal lattice. The efficiency and robustness of the algorithm are also investigated, leading to the development of modifications for enhanced performance.

A local ring $R$ is considered F-pure if its characteristic is non-two and it possesses certain properties related to its Frobenius endomorphism. The set of primes for which $R$ is F-pure is denoted as $\FP(R)$. If $\FP(R)$ contains all sufficiently large positive integers of a certain residue, the ring $R$ is considered to have a compact Hilbert polynomial. In studies of local domains with rational coefficients, sufficient conditions are established for both F-purity and the compact Hilbert property, which hold for rings exhibiting this latter characteristic in high enough characteristics. Nonetheless, an example is provided of a ring that possesses the compact Hilbert property but whose subring, which lacks this property, is not strictly included.

This paper puts forward a new framework for understanding auxiliary services procurement models. It is designed to incorporate market dynamics and influences when developing policies. Initially, it outlines key market factors that need consideration. Subsequently, it outlines strategic approaches to achieving optimal market outcomes. Finally, it offers a comprehensive set of policy guidelines. These can be applied across various markets and settings. Case studies are used to demonstrate the framework's applicability. They include the UK's planning system, UK gas distribution services, UK fire services, and UK railway signalling. The paper also encourages further research. It suggests expanding on existing studies and conducting new investigations. These should explore existing cases in greater depth, examine other services that fit the framework. Additionally, it would be useful to incorporate micro-foundations and psychological aspects into the model.

Given complex polynomials $P$ and $Q$ with degrees $d_P$ and $d_Q$, where $d_P < d_Q$, the paper proves that if $d_Q$ is not equal to $d_P$ times any rational number, then the prime factorization of compositions $P^{o_1}\circ (R\circ Q)^{o_2}$ for any polynomial $R$ occurs only finitely many times. Additionally, this result extends to semirective sequences of compositions and parallel compositions of polynomials.

This paper explores a new method for calculating the differential cross section of the Higgs boson pair production process, specifically in the bbWW* final state, using the matrix element technique. We employed MadGraph5_aMC@NLO to generate the 2-to-2 scattering process and obtained the relevant kinematic information, including the transverse momentum of the b-quark. By utilizing the generated data, we were able to replicate the transverse momentum distribution and compare our results to existing theoretical predictions, such as NNLL, NNLO, and LO. Our analysis revealed a significant improvement in the fit quality, reducing the $\chi^2$/Ndof value from an initial LO value of 20.6 to a final value of 5.57 after incorporating higher-order corrections, demonstrating the effectiveness of our method.

We utilize $e^+e^-\to Zh$ and the subsequent analysis of the final state, consisting of one visible Z and the photon pair from the Higgs boson decay, to set precise constraints on the Standard Model beyond its original formulation. By comparing theoretical predictions with experimental data from the CESR-SPEAR facility, we establish new, stringent limits on a variety of expanded scalar sector parameters. Specifically, we determine 95% confidence interval coefficients that reflect the range of these parameters where no observable deviation from the standard theory has been discovered. Notably, we've reduced the mass of a colorless scalar scalar by at least 276 MeV and enhanced the precision of another scalar's coupling to the Higgs by a factor of eight, reaching $0.126 \times \Gamma_{SM}$. Furthermore, we've set similar precise limits on the photon coupling of a second scalar, the dark photon coupling of both scalars, and a quartic self-interaction scalar coupling. These findings, once combined with data from $hadhhad$ collisions, will aid in identifying any expanded scalar sector.

Saturn's high-latitude atmosphere is dominated by rapid seasonal transformations.  Currently, solar radiation is reaching Saturn's north pole after six years of obstruction by the giant axial tilt.  Observations of total infrared light from Saturn show the start of a polar vortex development in Saturn's northern atmosphere, predicted to reach six meters per second speeds during the coming years.  Our new observations of thermal infrared and visible light reveal a large hexagonal pattern at six9 degrees latitude that encloses the high-speed winds area.  This structure likely formed to minimize the vortex's breakdown into smaller eddies.  Comparing these observations to simulations indicates a possible mechanism for generating such large hexagons during stable flow conditions around the vortex.  If this hypothesis holds, it could hold the key to understanding similar phenomena on Saturn and other planets with rich atmospheres.

For a specific nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an external potential in R^d, we will prove that under certain conditions, nontrivial solutions that explode at a convex boundary do not exist for energies lower than the boundary's potential energy. We will also establish sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of such solutions in scenarios where they may positively exist, including cases where they are evaluated at a spherical boundary for a star-shaped potential, and a specific case where they are evaluated at a parabolic boundary.

We introduce a novel class of mappings known as local-semantic (or local-chromatic) abbreviations, which serve as parameterized definitions of target spaces in positive-characteristic rings. These mappings enable the expression of complex geometric structures, like algebraic varieties, within lower-dimensional parameters. Notably, we have developed a new approach to localize-define target spaces using combinatorial and algebraic components, which demonstrates the capacity to represent complex structures within simpler, parameterized frameworks. This approach has significant implications for understanding the relationship between local-semantic abbreviations and other definition types, such as local-descriptive (or local-hued) abbreviations.

The behavior of V$_2$O$_3$ thin films changes at a critical thickness, and to study the metal-insulator transition, understanding this shift in thinner layers is vital. Researchers have various explanations for this shift, including the influence of surface conditions. In this research, surface modifications such as oxygen exposure and sodium doping were removed to gain deeper insights. Unexpectedly, thinner film samples displayed an insulating surface condition, and their bulk properties were influenced by surface treatments. Notably, oxygen exposure led to a metal-like surface in thicker film samples.

We examined how two quantum double dark solitons, created through various interactions and scattering patterns, maintain their shape and gradually blend into one another.  Our study used both one-dimensional and two-component models and employed high-precision numbers for their properties.  We found that certain types of collisions cause internal vibrations, while others use solitonic patterns to mix together.  Furthermore, our research found a link between these patterns and what's known as 'gray solitons'.  In addition, we developed a new method for scaling out the effects of size in two-component systems, finding it matched closely with direct simulations.  Our study also looked at how dark-bright solitons behave under different collisions and found both signs of vibrational effects and g-factor induced gray solitons.  These findings may be useful for experiments to look for dark-bright solitons.

Given a field $\kappa$ and positive integer $d$, a graded collection $\mathcal{F}$ over $\kappa$ comprises objects $\mathcal{F}_i$ indexed from $0$ to $d$, each defined over $\kappa^i$. This paper introduces the notion of polarization, which associates to $\mathcal{F}$ a new collection $\mathrm{Pol}(\mathcal{ F})$ over $\kappa$. The indexing of $\mathrm{Pol}(\mathcal{ F})$ spans from $0$ to $d+1$, with $\mathrm{Pol}(\mathcal{ F})_i$ depending directly on $\mathcal{F}_{i-1}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{i+1}$ for $0<i<d+1$. Constructs like linear spaces, vector bundles, and their numbered variants admit well-defined polarization operations. We showcase the role of polarization in establishing an invariant for grouped schemes that remains unchanged under equivalence, and introduce the concept of degeneration to normal crossing as another application of polarization.

We establish the compatibility of orbital integrals with standardizations of measures at the level of orbital integrals for a specific class of orbital integrals known as Weyl group elements. This standardization-based relationship facilitates comparing measures across different standardizations and, under certain conditions, demonstrates their consistency. These features can support the implementation of orbital integrals in the context of the geometric Satake isomorphism.

We have conducted calculations showing that the nuclear phase of Sca-sia-2008, which was previously thought to be a quantum critical point, is a distinct quantum critical point that is associated with a change in bond-angle symmetry from $C_4$ to $C_2$. Our analysis indicates that the SC gap in this state is significantly larger than that in other SC states and suggests the existence of additional order in the Sca-2008 state. We have also proposed using x-ray scattering to verify this additional order.

Advanced quantum error correction codes, such as the surface code, are crucial for building functional quantum computers. From an electrical engineering standpoint, it is necessary to determine the minimum level of noise resistance in quantum circuits that connect qubits. However, most current studies on code thresholds do not fully capture the constraints imposed by imperfect classical control systems. We examine a mathematical model of an isotropic quantum tripartite graph code and develop a probabilistic framework to analyze its error stability. This lead research restricts quantum code threshold analysis to a well-defined parameter and develop analogous code performance criteria to the Ising model's phase transition concepts. These conditions are then used to establish the noise resistance limits for quantum circuits employing the honeycomb code.

Recent theoretical predictions have highlighted a range of atomically thin materials with exceptional properties, including topological characteristics and multi-fold degenerate states. However, these predictions lack experimental verification. In this study, we present a experimental realization of topologically active, gap-rich tellurene. Through first principles calculations, we identified five distinct families of stabilized, flat-band, atomically flat Te-Te interfaces. Among these, the beta phase exhibited the largest band gap (~1.0 eV) and exhibited Haldane-like topological properties. We discovered that it is possible to induce a topological phase transition in this phase by doping it with alkali metals or altering its strain. Moreover, we demonstrated that certain stabilized variants of tellurene can exhibit exceptional TQFT response when doped with electron holes.

We propose a novel numerical method to solve single-phase Darcy flow in a rock formation containing discontinuities. This method combines the discrete weak formulation with the hybrid mixed finite element technique. It permits precise representation of complex fracture networks within a physical domain, utilizing a grid that aligns with the cracks. The core approach is to estimate the fluid pressure at specific points of the domain, leveraging a rich set of basis functions developed from the characteristic properties of the fractures. This method leverages a discontinuous pressure field in the domain between cracks and applies a well-established mixed finite element technique in each sub-region. Our numerical experiments demonstrate the method's efficiency, versatility, and adaptability to a wide range of fracture permeability distributions. This technique overcomes limitations of traditional hybrid mixed finite element methods, which struggle with complex fracture geometries requiring global enrichment of the basis set, such as in the GPDM technique.

The concept of Bayes Factors has significant potential in moving away from p-hacking towards more rigorous statistical testing, but adopting this approach on a large scale poses computational challenges. To overcome this, we've developed a statistical testing workflow that can be executed on high-performance computing systems. By utilizing Bayes Factors, this approach is capable of running numerous comparative analyses simultaneously, even with complex, intractable models. We've demonstrated the effectiveness of this workflow by conducting a large-scale analysis of neural network interpretations and linguistic data, computing Bayes Factors for competing models across many conditions or datasets. The results indicate successful detection of both significant differences and models that perform comparably. Furthermore, we propose using Bayes Factors in combination with other decision theories to make data-driven choices, but further investigation is required to fully explore this combination.

Standard NLP tasks NLP models typically ignore the function of discourse markers,
which are words that manage communication between people. This is because
current models do not fully capture how native speakers use these words to
convey meaning. As a result, they struggle to produce natural language when
these models are applied to generate text. To address this issue, our proposed
approach, DiscSense, is a method for assessing the implicit meaning of discourse
markers behind them. We devised a step-by-step evaluation measure that relies on
downstream task performance of the sentences preceded by these markers. To test
this method, we created a comprehensive dataset covering 10 different discourse
marker items and 8 NLP tasks. Our results indicate that pre-trained BERT models
that are trained with specialized discourse indicators outperform their base
models across most evaluation tasks. Notably, the discourse-aware models achieved
better performance than random chance in 19 out of 24 instances, and were capable
of surpassing their respective base models in 10 instances.

We investigated the effects of elevated temperatures on optical absorption and photoluminescence in a specific range (up to 873 K) for a material containing a defect known as "nitrogen vacancy" in a diamond sample.  A specific excitation and emission technique at room temperature was used to track changes in zero-phonon line positions and intensities for red and green emissions.  The results showed that a red emission shift pattern resembles previously observed behavior up to 443 K, but diverges beyond that temperature range, and the pattern is more pronounced in intensity than what has been reported in literature.  Additionally, the green emission shifts in a linear fashion with increasing temperature at a rate of 0.079 ± 0.005 eV/1000 K.  To explore the impact of nitrogen site orientation on emission shift patterns, a simulation based on first principles was utilized, and the experimental and theoretical results were compared, revealing a connection between the nitrogen site orientation and the emission shift pattern above 443 K.  The study also provides an updated analysis of activation energies and degeneracy for competing charge states in a material, and these findings have significant implications for emission stability in thermoluminescence dosimetry and temperature sensing at high temperatures.

The brain's cortical network utilizes areas of specialized function that are managed through self-regulating feedback loops. These self-regulating areas, which are monitored by surrounding neurons called surround inhibition, ensure the stability of neural activity. In this research, a neural network model was developed that utilizes a central-neuron/ surround-inhibition motif to manage the global dynamics of an encoded network. The model demonstrated that it could effectively monitor and manage the network's activity without needing external regulation, while also successfully achieving intrinsic stability, a key feature of functional specialized brain regions. Furthermore, neural network models that incorporate this central-neuron/ surround-inhibition motif exhibit a unique capacity to utilize both excitatory and inhibitory neurons to their full potential, while also demonstrating enhanced robustness to model variations.

Investigating SU(3) spin systems on a triangular lattice, we utilized the SU(3) triomer operator to assess the strength of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations. Monte Carlo simulations, employed to evaluate these correlations in various spin states (j), revealed significant differences between j≤4 and higher values of j. Specifically, for j>4, the results indicated non-zero antiferromagnetic tendencies. To further validate this finding, we applied an exact diagonalization technique and examined the energy gaps between the ground state and first excited state.

We present an innovative implementation of the HF method that utilizes a flexible B-spline framework to model random central potentials. By representing the HF equations in terms of spatial B-spline functions and parameterized potential, our approach enables efficient and adaptable computations. We've developed a suite of benchmarks including atoms with one valence electron, alkaline earth atoms, molecular aggregates, and a 2D 2-component planar system under an external field. These benchmarks demonstrate the versatility and versatility of our B-spline HF framework, yielding highly accurate results that align with high-precision experiments and theoretical predictions. Our method exhibits superior performance in terms of speed and flexibility, allowing for flexible basis optimizations and strikingly precise total energy calculations. Notably, our implemantation is entirely based on first-principles, allowing for a nuanced exploration of electronic systems across diverse frameworks.

The time-expectation standard, which identifies the typical occurrence time of a regular event, has been widely employed in mathematics and engineering. Herein, we expand this concept to encompass random processes and complex phenomena, particularly those involving interconnected oscillators. Building upon this extension, we create a novel standard for the explosive synchronization transition, which marks a sudden shift from quiescent behavior to coherent motion in oscillator networks. We generate an explicit standard expression for an $N$-dimensional damped and driven Kuramoto network and utilize it to identify the critical point of the transition, which can be experimentally verified. Additionally, we collect extensive time-series data from multiple network states and demonstrate that our standard metric, when plotted against a probability distribution, exhibits universal characteristics that are specific to the state of synchronization and resistant to variations in parameters. Our work signifies the beginning of using time-expectation standards to study dynamic systems and suggests that similar standards can be developed for other phenomena, such as onsets and transitions.

Low-rank matrix optimization problems are extensively utilized in a diverse range of applications and have numerous connections to various fields of study. A significant challenge associated with these problems lies in their non-convex nature, prompting numerous studies to analyze their global optimality landscapes and verify their efficacy in practical applications. A key insight from previous research suggests that restricting optimization to the manifold of positive definite matrices can transform these problems from being non-convex to geodesically convex, thus facilitating more efficient and accurate solutions. This study significantly advances this insight by comprehensively exploring and analyzing convex optimization from a Riemannian geometric perspective, addressing limitations of earlier studies that solely focused on local geometry. Our research suggests that transforming an arbitrary convex optimization problem into a geodesically convex one, as suggested by previous research, may not be as straightforward as it seems, suggesting a more nuanced understanding of this phenomenon. A key aspect of our research involves introducing a novel optimization framework that integrates low-rank and factorized matrix representations, allowing for more efficient and effective solutions. Our proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art algorithms, exhibiting faster and more reliable performance across a diverse range of experiments, suggesting a significant improvement in matrix factorization and completion problems.

In a recent study by Balogh, Bese, and Schrauter in 2019, the concept of edge-chirality was explored and it was demonstrated that certain graphs, including bipartite cubic graphs, can be robustly colored with five colors so that adjacent edges always have differing color pairs. We now show that a specific bipartite cubic graph cannot be accurately colored in this manner, thereby providing a counterexample to the conjecture posed in that research.

Let $p$ be an odd prime and $q(\cdot)$ denote the Dirichlet character modulo $p$. For any prime $r \not= p$, we establish the following identities:
$$
\sum_{n \bmod r} q(n) \log | \eta_n | = -\frac{\pi}{4r} \sum_{s \bmod r} | \sum_{n \bmod r} \bar{q}(n) \log (s-n)_r |,
$$
and
$$
\sum_{n \bmod r} \bar{q}(n) \log | \eta_n | = -\frac{\pi}{4r} \sum_{s \bmod r} | \sum_{n \bmod r} \bar{q}(n^{-1}) \log (s-n)_r |,
$$
where $\eta_n = \prod_{j=1}^{(r-1)/2} (s-j)_r (s-j^{-1})_r$. These equations represent novel relationships between the Gauss sums $\tau(q)$ and the residues of the Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(1, \bar{q})$. Additionally, we provide a numerical verification for specific primes $r$.

New physics beyond the Standard Model may be revealed through high-energy particles at the Large Hadron Collider and very high energy cosmic rays. We explore a new way to achieve this by connecting particles and forces with external fields that change over time and space, such as neutrinos that oscillate with a gravitational wave. This new framework allows for stable or short-lived particles with extremely high masses. We can produce these particles in the laboratory with Neutrino factories or in the upper atmosphere with extremely high energy photons and neutrons generated in "graveyard" asteroids by dark radiation. Even if these particles decay quickly, they could influence the evolution of the universe and provide a signature in the large scale structure of the universe and the cosmic microwave background.

Swimming in a complex, viscoelastic fluid environment is affected by its specific rheological properties in a non-intuitive manner. Our study utilizes both computational modeling and experimental methods to investigate the influence of viscoelasticity on the swimming speed and orientation of a dual-asymmetry swimmer. By comparing swimmers with symmetric front-rear designs to those with asymmetrical front-rear designs, we discover that viscoelasticity induces twisting swimming behavior in the latter. Further analysis reveals that viscoelasticity's impact is heavily dependent on the viscoelastic number and that a viscoelastic fluid causes the latter swimmer to perform a figure-eight swimming pattern under certain conditions. Notably, we observe that this viscoelastic-induced twisting helps the swimmer achieve higher speeds in viscoelastic fluids, in contrast to fluids with Newtonian properties.

We investigated a variety of coevolutionary genetic algorithms that employ populations of strategies to solve the double-orphan mechanism for Nash equilibrium in a two-player symmetric Cournot game. Our research revealed that while some evolutionary methods are capable of converging to the optimal solution, most introduce excessive uncertainty due to changes in population size, selection mechanisms, and mutation rates, ultimately yielding only suboptimal results.

As the size of ontologies continues to expand, traditional development methods are no longer fully effective, especially given the significant potential for leveraging large-scale web data to enrich ontologies.  Though numerous automatic or semi-automatic techniques exist for generating new concepts and relationships, a unified framework that encompasses all aspects of ontology learning from raw text is lacking.  In addition, existing approaches are often specialized and require substantial human input to integrate results into existing ontologies.  We present a unified deep learning framework that encompasses all aspects of ontology learning from disorganized text, including the implicit extraction of entity attributes.  Notably, our framework includes the use of a specialized neural network component based on the BERT model.  Experiments conducted on the Wikipedia ontology dataset indicate that the framework can outperform human annotators in precision for certain concept categories and compete with state-of-the-art methods for entity attributes and ontology structures.  Further experiments performed on the GeoNames ontology demonstrate that the framework can generate high-quality concepts and attributes, and these results can complement or surpass existing ontology data in quality.

A new statistical equilibrium framework for isolated systems far from their crystalline ground state has been devised, based on the free energy and a generalized temperature concept. This framework is illustrated with a novel model of Ising-doped Drude systems on fully connected graphs, and exact matches with experimental measurements of conductance and temperature are achieved. On a nonequilibrium basis, a generalized conductance and temperature equation of state can also be derived, deviating from the classical form.
